children.text: māhātmyametadvṛṣabhadhvajasya śrutvā muner gandhavatīsutasya
children.translated_text: Having heard this greatness of the bull-bannered lord from the sage, the son of Gandhavatī,

children.text: vaco mahārthaṃ munayaśca sarve papracchur ugraṃ praṇipatya sūtam ||
children.translated_text: all the sages bowed down to the formidable Sūta and asked him a question of great import.

children.text: munaya ūcuḥ
children.translated_text: The sages said:

children.text: kimandhakārirbhagavān pinākī kasyānvaye vīryavataḥ pṛthivyām
children.translated_text: In what lineage on earth was the blessed <s>Pinākin</s>, the enemy of <s>Andhaka</s>, born, mighty and heroic?

children.text: jāto mahātmā balavān pradhāne kaścāndhakaḥ kasya sutaḥ kathaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: And who was <s>Andhaka</s>, whose son was he, and how did this great-souled, powerful one arise in the chief line?

children.text: etat samagraṃ sarahasyamadya bravīhi sūta bhagavatprasādāt
children.translated_text: Tell us all this today, together with its secret meaning, O <s>Sūta</s>, by the grace of the Lord.

children.text: vyāsāt tvayā vai viditaṃ hi samyag yuddhaṃ yathābhūd anayor hataḥ saḥ ||
children.translated_text: For you have learned fully from <s>Vyāsa</s> how the battle between these two took place and how he was slain.

children.text: teṣāṃ tadāsau vacanaṃ niśamya provāca sūtastu munīṃstadānīm
children.translated_text: Hearing their words then, <s>Sūta</s> spoke at that time to the sages:

children.text: pūrvaṃ dvijā mandaraśailasaṃsthā kaparddinaścaṇḍaparākramasya ||
children.translated_text: Formerly, O twice-born ones, on Mount <s>Mandara</s>, of the matted-haired lord of fierce valor,

children.text: cakre tato netranimīlanaṃ tu sā pārvvatī narmayutaṃ salīlam
children.translated_text: <s>Pārvatī</s>, playful and smiling, then closed his eyes,

children.text: pravālahemābjadhṛtaprabhābhyāṃ karāmbujābhyāṃ nimimīla netre ||
children.translated_text: covering the eyes with her lotus-like hands, bright like coral, gold, and lotuses.

children.text: harasya netreṣu nimīliteṣu kṣaṇena jātaḥ sumahāndhakāraḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Hara</s>'s eyes were closed, in an instant a very great darkness arose.

children.text: tatsparśayogācca maheśvarasya karācca tasyāḥ skhalitaṃ madāmbhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And from the contact with <s>Maheśvara</s>, a drop of sweat slipped from her hand.

children.text: śambhorlalāṭekṣaṇavahnitapto vinirgato bhūrijalasya binduḥ
children.translated_text: Heated by the fire of <s>Śambhu</s>'s forehead-eye, a drop of abundant moisture came forth,

children.text: garbho babhūvātha karānanasya bhayaṅkaraḥ krodhaparaḥ kṛtaghnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and from the hand and mouth there arose a fetus, terrifying, wrathful, and ungrateful.

children.text: anyo virūpī jaṭilaḥ śmaśrulaśca kṛṣṇo naro vai vikṛtaḥ suromā
children.translated_text: Another being appeared, deformed, matted-haired, bearded, black, misshapen, and very hairy,

children.text: gāyan hasan prarudan nṛtyamāno vilelihāno ghanaghoraghoṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: singing, laughing, weeping, dancing, licking about, with a deep and dreadful roar.

children.text: jātena tenādbhutadarśanena gaurīṃ bhavo'sau smitapūrvam āha
children.translated_text: When that wondrous-looking being had been born, <s>Bhava</s> said to <s>Gaurī</s> with a smile:

children.text: nimīlya netrāṇi kṛtaṃ ca narma vibheṣase māṃ dayite kathaṃ tvam ||
children.translated_text: 'Beloved, you closed my eyes in play; how is it that you are frightened of me?'

children.text: gaurī harāt tadvacanaṃ niśamya vihasyamānā pramumoca netre
children.translated_text: Hearing those words of <s>Hara</s>, <s>Gaurī</s> laughed and opened his eyes.

children.text: jāte prakāśe sati ghorarūpo jāto'ndhakārādapi netrahīnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When light had appeared, the dreadful-formed one, born from darkness, was also eyeless.

children.text: papraccha ko'yaṃ bhagavan virūpas tādṛgvidhaṃ tacca nirīkṣya bhūtam
children.translated_text: Seeing that being of such a kind, she asked, 'Blessed lord, who is this deformed one?

children.text: vadasva satyaṃ mama kiṃ nimittaṃ sṛṣṭo'thavā kena ca kasya puttraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tell me truly: for what reason was he created, or by whom, and whose son is he?'

children.text: śrutvā harastadvacanaṃ priyāyā utpanna eṣo'dbhutacaṇḍavīryyaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing those words of his beloved, <s>Hara</s> said, 'This being of wondrous and fierce valor has arisen.

children.text: nimīlite cakṣuṣī me bhavatyā sa svedajaścāndhakanāmadheyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When my eyes were closed by you, he was born from sweat and is named <s>Andhaka</s>.

children.text: tato'sya kartāsmi yathānurūpaṃ tvayā sasakhyā sadayaṃ gaṇebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore I am his maker in due form. Together with your friends, with compassion, among the gaṇas,

children.text: sa rakṣitavyas tvayanaṃ hi caikaṃ vicārya buddhyā karaṇīyam ārye ||
children.translated_text: he is to be protected by you. This one thing must indeed be done, noble lady, after considering it with wisdom.'

children.text: gaurī tato bharttṛvaco niśamya kāruṇyabhāvāt sahitā sakhībhiḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Gaurī</s>, hearing her husband's words, out of compassion and accompanied by her companions,

children.text: nānāprakārair bahubhir hyupāyaiścakāra rakṣāṃ svasutasya yadvat ||
children.translated_text: protected him by many different means, just as one protects one's own son.

children.text: kāle'tha yasmin bhuvi cāndhakastu hiraṇyanetrastvatha putrakāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Now at the time when <s>Andhaka</s> was on earth, <s>Hiraṇyanetra</s>, desiring a son,

children.text: araṇyam āśritya tapaścakāra jātastadā kaśyapajaḥ sutārtham ||
children.translated_text: a son of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, resorted to the forest and performed austerity for the sake of a son.

children.text: kāṣṭhopamo'sau jitaroṣadoṣaḥ saṃdarśanārthaṃ tu maheśvarasya
children.translated_text: Like a piece of wood, having conquered the fault of anger, he sought the sight of <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: tuṣṭaḥ pinākī tapasāsya samanyag varapradānāya yayau dvijendrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Pleased by his austerity, <s>Pinākin</s> went to grant him a boon, O best of twice-born ones.

children.text: tuṣṭastamāhākulitendriyaṃ taṃ kimartham etadvratam āśritaṃ te
children.translated_text: Pleased, he said to that man whose senses were agitated, 'For what purpose have you undertaken this vow?

children.text: prabrūhi kāmaṃ varado bhavo'haṃ yad icchasi tvaṃ sakalaṃ dadāmi ||
children.translated_text: Declare your desire. I am <s>Bhava</s>, the giver of boons; whatever you wish, I will give it all.'

children.text: puttrastu me candralalāṭa nāsti suvīryavān daityakulānurūpī
children.translated_text: 'Moon-crested lord, I have no son, no very heroic one suited to the daitya race.

children.text: tadarthametad vratam āsthito'haṃ taṃ dehi deveśa suvīryyavantam ||
children.translated_text: For that purpose I have undertaken this vow. Give me such a son, O lord of gods, one very full of valor.

children.text: yasmācca madbhrāturanantavīryyāḥ prahrādapūrvā api pañca puttrāḥ
children.translated_text: For my brother has five sons of endless valor, beginning with <s>Prahrāda</s>,

children.text: mameha nāstīti niranvayo'haṃ yo māmakaṃ rājyamidaṃ bubhūṣet ||
children.translated_text: but I have none here; thus I am without lineage, with no one who would desire this kingdom of mine.

children.text: rāṣṭraṃ parasya svabalena hṛtvā bhuṅkte'thavā svaṃ pitureva diṣṭam
children.translated_text: One who, by his own strength, seizes another's realm and enjoys it, or enjoys the paternal realm assigned to him,

children.text: sa procyate puttra ihāpyamutra puttrī sa tenāpi bhavet pitāsau ||
children.translated_text: is called a son here and hereafter; by him even the father becomes possessed of a son.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ gatiḥ puttravatāṃ niruktā manīṣibhir dharmavatāṃ variṣṭhaiḥ
children.translated_text: The upward course of those who have sons has been taught by wise men, the foremost among the righteous.

children.text: sarvāṇi bhūtāni tadarthameva mṛtau pravartanti haṭhāt svabhāvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: All beings, by their very nature, are forcibly active at death for that very purpose.

children.text: niranvayasyāpi na santi lokās tadarthamicchanti sutān svabhūmne
children.translated_text: For one without descendants there are no worlds; therefore men desire sons for their own welfare.

children.text: krītādayaḥ santi sutāstathāṣṭau icchāmi tasmāt sutam ekameva ||
children.translated_text: There are eight kinds of sons, such as the purchased son; therefore I desire just one son.'

children.text: etadbhavastadvacanaṃ niśamya kṛpākaro daityanṛpasya tuṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing these words, <s>Bhava</s>, compassionate and pleased with the king of the daityas,

children.text: tamāha daityādhipa nāsti puttras tvadvīryyajaḥ kiṃtu dadāmi puttram ||
children.translated_text: said to him, 'Lord of daityas, there is no son born from your own virility, but I shall give you a son.

children.text: mamātmajaṃ tvandhakanāmadheyaṃ tvattulyavīryyaṃ hyaparājitaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Take my own son, named <s>Andhaka</s>, equal to you in valor and unconquered.

children.text: vṛṇīṣva puttraṃ sakalaṃ vihāya duḥkhaṃ pratīcchasva sukhaṃ hi cemam ||
children.translated_text: Choose this son, abandon all sorrow, and accept this happiness.'

children.text: ityevamuktvā pradadau sa tasmai hiraṇyanetrāya sutaṃ prasannaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, he gladly gave the son to <s>Hiraṇyanetra</s>.

children.text: harastu gauryā sahito mahātmā bhūtādhināthastripurārirugraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hara</s>, the great-souled lord of beings, the fierce enemy of <s>Tripura</s>, was together with <s>Gaurī</s>.

children.text: tato harāt prāpya sutaṃ sa daityaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya yathākrameṇa
children.translated_text: Then, having received the son from <s>Hara</s>, that daitya circumambulated him in due order,

children.text: stotrair anekairabhipūjya rudraṃ hṛṣṭaḥ svarājyaṃ gatavān mahātmā ||
children.translated_text: worshiped <s>Rudra</s> with many hymns, and, delighted, the great-souled one went to his own kingdom.

children.text: tatastu puttraṃ giriśād avāpya rasātalaṃ caṇḍaparākramastu
children.translated_text: Then, having obtained the son from <s>Giriśa</s>, the daitya of fierce valor went to <s>Rasātala</s>,

children.text: imāṃ dharitrīmanayat svadeśaṃ daityo vijitya tridaśānaśeṣān ||
children.translated_text: and after conquering all the gods without remainder, he brought this earth under his own dominion.

children.text: tatastu devairmunibhiśca sarvaiḥ sarvātmakaṃ yajñamayaṃ karālam
children.translated_text: Then by all the gods and sages, the terrible one, consisting of all and made of sacrifice,

children.text: vārāhamāśritya vapuḥ pradhānam ārādhito viṣṇur anantavīryyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having taken on the chief boar body, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whose power is endless, was worshipped.

children.text: ghoṇāprahārair vividhairdharitrīṃ vidārya pātālatalaṃ praviśya
children.translated_text: With various blows of his snout he split the earth and, entering the surface of the underworld,

children.text: tuṇḍena daityān śataśo vicūrṇya daṃṣṭrābhir agryābhir akhaṇḍitābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: with his muzzle he crushed demons by the hundreds, with his foremost, unbroken tusks.

children.text: pādaprahārair aśaniprakāśair unmathya sainyāni niśācarāṇām
children.translated_text: With foot-blows that shone like thunderbolts, he churned up the armies of the night-roamers;

children.text: mārtaṇḍakoṭipratimena paścāt sudarśanenādbhutacaṇḍatejāḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, with the <s>Sudarśana</s>, equal to ten million suns, he possessed wondrous and fierce splendor.

children.text: hiraṇyanetrasya śiro jvalantaṃ cicheda daityāṃśca dadāha duṣṭān
children.translated_text: He cut off the blazing head of <s>Hiraṇyanetra</s> and burned the wicked demons.

children.text: tataḥ prahṛṣṭo ditijendrarājye tamandhakaṃ tatra sa cābhyaṣiñcat ||
children.translated_text: Then, delighted, he consecrated that <s>Andhaka</s> there in the kingdom of the lord of the descendants of <s>Diti</s>.

children.text: svasthānam āsādya tato dharitrīṃ daṃṣṭrāṅkureṇādadharat prahṛṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: Afterward, having reached his own place, delighted, he held up the earth on the tip of his tusk;

children.text: bhūmiṃ ca pātālatalānmahātmā pupoṣa bhāgaṃ tvatha pūrvakaṃ tu ||
children.translated_text: and the great-souled one nourished the earth from the surface of the underworld, its former portion indeed.

children.text: pratāpya lokānakhilāṃstato'sau samāgataḥ padmayoniṃ dadarśa
children.translated_text: After scorching all the worlds, he then came and saw the lotus-born one,

children.text: varaṃ pradātuṃ pravadantameva varaṃ vṛṇīṣveti sa mūḍhabuddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: who was speaking in order to grant a boon: "Choose a boon." But he was of deluded mind.

children.text: mṛtyor bhayaṃ me bhagavan sadaiva pitāmahābhūnna kadācidevam
children.translated_text: "Lord, fear of death has always existed for me. Grandfather, let it never be so,

children.text: śastrāstrapāśāśaniśuṣkavṛkṣagirīndratoyāgniripuprahāraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: from weapons, missiles, nooses, thunderbolts, dry trees, lordly mountains, water, fire, or the blows of enemies;

children.text: svarge dharaṇyāṃ divase niśāyāṃ daivāhataḥ prāha na so'pi sandhau
children.translated_text: in heaven or on earth, by day or by night, struck by fate." Nor did he speak even of twilight.

children.text: tasyaitadīdṛgvacanaṃ niśamya daityendra tuṣṭo'smi labhasva sarvam ||
children.translated_text: Having heard this speech of his of such a kind, he said, "Lord of demons, I am pleased; obtain everything."

children.text: praṇamya viṣṇuṃ manasā tamāha bhayānvito'sāvapi padmayoniḥ
children.translated_text: Bowing mentally to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the lotus-born one, though himself afraid, said to him:

children.text: tataḥ sa daityaḥ paripūrṇakāmastvam aṣṭakoṭyastvatha ṣaṇṇavatyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Then, demon, your desires are fulfilled; you shall have ninety-six plus eight crores."

children.text: uttiṣṭha rājyaṃ kuru dānavānāṃ śrutvā giraṃ tāṃ sa sukhī babhūva
children.translated_text: "Rise; rule the kingdom of the demons." Hearing that speech, he became happy.

children.text: rājye'bhiṣiktaḥ prapitāmahena trailokyanāśāya matiṃ cakāra ||
children.translated_text: Consecrated in the kingdom by his great-grandfather, he set his mind on the destruction of the three worlds.

children.text: utsādya dharmmān sakalān pramatto jitvāhave so'pi surān samastān
children.translated_text: Mad with pride, having uprooted all <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) and having conquered all the gods in battle,

children.text: tato bhayād indramukhāśca devāḥ kṣīrodadhau yatra haristu śete ||
children.translated_text: then the gods, with <s>Indra</s> at their head, out of fear went to the milk ocean where <s>Hari</s> sleeps.

children.text: ārādhayāmāsur atīva gatvā tatastu hṛṣṭaḥ pradadau varāṃstu
children.translated_text: Having gone there, they worshipped him intensely; then, pleased, he granted boons.

children.text: utthāya tasmācchayanād upendro yathānurūpair vividhair vacobhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Rising from that couch, <s>Upendra</s>, with various words suited to the occasion,

children.text: āśvāsya devānakhilān munīndrā ravīnduvaiśvānaratulyatejāḥ
children.translated_text: reassured all the gods and the foremost sages, being equal in splendor to sun, moon, and fire.

children.text: āśritya rūpaṃ jaṭilaṃ karālaṃ daṃṣṭrāyudhaṃ tīkṣṇanakhaṃ sunāsam ||
children.translated_text: He assumed a form matted-haired, terrible, armed with tusks, sharp-clawed, and well-nosed,

children.text: mṛgendratulyaṃ ca vidāritāsyaṃ mārtaṇḍakoṭipratimaṃ sughoram
children.translated_text: like the lord of beasts, with gaping mouth, equal to ten million suns, exceedingly dreadful,

children.text: yugāntakālāgnisamaprabhāvaṃ jaganmayaṃ kiṃ bahubhirvacobhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: with power like the fire at the end of an age, pervading the world; what need is there of many words?

children.text: astaṃ ravau so'pi hi gacchamāne gato'surāṇāṃ nagarīṃ mahātmā
children.translated_text: As the sun was setting, that great-souled one went to the city of the demons;

children.text: kṛtvā ca yuddhaṃ prabalaiḥ sahāyair hatvātha tān daityagaṇān grahītum ||
children.translated_text: and, having waged battle with his mighty helpers and having then slain those hosts of demons, he set out to seize him.
